headline: New Zealand exports performing well despite tariff increase to 12.5%, with beef and wine demand remaining strong in the US
reasoning: Brad Gordon notes New Zealand's tariff rate moved from 10% to 12.5%, in line with Australia, but does not view this as a significant issue. The main drag on the economy is domestic housing rather than trade.

headline: New Zealand facing macro headwinds from higher interest rates and weak domestic housing, particularly in Auckland and Wellington
reasoning: Brad Gordon notes that confidence in Auckland is not strong, with inflation running higher and interest rates elevated. When the five-year swap rate exceeds 4%, he observes a grind and slowdown in economic activity. He attributes much of this to offshore factors including higher US bond rates, noting New Zealand is particularly sensitive to these dynamics. Domestic housing remains very tough, especially in the North Island, with Auckland house prices down approximately 35% from their highs.
quote: Look I mean I don't think you can say particularly in Auckland here that confidence is going through the roof. Um inflation came out high last week and or two weeks ago. And um interest rates are hitting higher. It seems to be when the five year swap rate exceeds 4%. You do see a bit of a grind and a slowdown. And that's what's happened. Unfortunately, it's not really New Zealand's fault. Um, it's a lot of offshore factors, including bond rates hitting higher and, um, in the US. But New Zealand does seem to be more sensitive to that.
